source_text: Verumtamen, ad destructionem totam dogmatis tui proficit, ut etiam recordemur definitionum superiorum. Si peccatum non est nisi voluntas retinendi et admittendi, quod iustitia vetat et unde liberum est abstinere, nullum peccatum in rebus penitus invenitur.
pass_a_gloss: Nevertheless, it profits toward the whole destruction of your dogma, that we also remember the upper definitions. If sin is not unless a will of retaining and admitting, what justice forbids and from which it is free to abstain, no sin at all is found in things.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS liber=free; Blaise unde liberum est abstinere

pass_b_english: Recalling our earlier definitions, however, also helps demolish your doctrine completely. If sin is nothing but the will to retain and commit what justice forbids and from which one is free to abstain, then on your account no sin can be found anywhere in reality.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

variants.reading: “On your account” makes explicit that Julian is drawing a consequence from Augustine’s position, not denying that sin exists.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
